cards.when: Both are for a WORLD CHANGE: clip to clip, plate to plate, page to a different page.

cards.title: The melt scene exit
cards.does: Only the outgoing chart's ink sags, fuses and compiles on 2s into a dense heavy ball while the board stays; then one of three authored endings.

author.key: shot row 6th element 'melt[:throw|:splash:chart|:splash:plate][:weight[:<material>]][:depth=<k>][:<s>][:<x>,<y>]' (validator: parse_exit (via scene_exit); melt boundaries: stamp_transition_pages/_melt_boundary)

phases.name: sag
phases.does: the chart's ink (never the board) smears downward in offset copies under the gooey threshold and fuses; its box outline grows seeded drips and slumps
phases.trigger: the scene boundary (u = 0 of the exit window)

phases.name: ball
phases.does: on the stepped clock (on 2s) the ink squeezes to its centroid while the outline morphs to a circle and an opaque K-M-concentrated body grows over it

phases.name: ending
phases.does: one of three authored endings - throw | splash:chart | splash:plate (see melt_ending rows)

phases.name: weight
phases.does: the ball lands, rolls without slipping (the turn IS the distance over the radius), takes one nudge sold before it moves, and settles - its surface Rayleigh's modes, its ink mark turning with it, its highlight on the light
phases.trigger: u = BALL_END of what is left (the ball's end), on `melt:weight` only

phases.name: gone
phases.does: the outgoing world, its ink and the overlay are hidden

blends.source: stop-action stepped clock, impactSquash and throwXf (kinetics/stopaction.mjs)
four laws we already owned, chained (R26-15's melt lesson)

options.means: The melt at a depth: melt:...:depth=<k> puts the ink clone and the ball overlay on the camera read at k (camLayerCss), so the ball melts, lands and is thrown at that plane.
The melt's own length: The melt runs over the seconds its suffix declares instead of its default dial.
The melt: splash into the next chart: The ink ball splatters back onto the board and the splatter forms the next chart, which arrives built.
The melt: splash that paints a plate: The ink ball splatters and a narrative plate springs up out of it, reading as painted by that ink.
The melt: thrown off: The ink ball is thrown off the stage and the next chart draws on the same board.
The melt: the ball has MASS - it lands, rolls without slipping (its ink mark turning), is nudged and settles, its surface the living drop. Opt-in `melt:weight[:<material>]`, metal by default.

lives.note: MELT / MELT_ENDINGS / meltOpts (engine glue: paintMelt, meltMount, clearMelt)

callable.why: compiles; the R26-76 rework's look pass 3 was accepted on the parent's frame read 2026-09-13 but is uncommitted and awaits the operator's watch in motion; bare melt:splash refused

cards.title: The slide scene exit
cards.does: The incoming frame pushes the outgoing one off the stage along one axis, both moving together by the same distance over SLIDE_S, each clipped to its own stage rect, so the two frames abut at every instant.
cards.when: A HAND-OFF, not a world-taking transition: when the next world should read as the same picture carried on - chart to chart on the same board - so the two worlds stay spatially continuous.

author.key: shot row 6th element 'slide:<left|right|up|down>' or 'slide:<dir>:<s>' (validator: parse_exit (via scene_exit); the direction is never defaulted and `push` is refused by name)

phases.name: the push
phases.does: the outgoing world travels sign * u * the stage's span and the incoming world (u - 1) * the same span, on min-jerk, each clipped to its own stage rect - one distance, opposite ends, so the two frames abut at every u
phases.trigger: the scene boundary (a slide arrives on the cut, like the suck and the melt)

phases.name: the landing
phases.does: the outgoing frame is exactly off the stage and the incoming one stands at its own place; the page it hands to has been building on its axes throughout

blends.source: @remotion/transitions' `slide` presentation (the editor already imports the package - editor/src/TransitionEvidence60sProof.tsx)
blends.became: the geometry: the enter and the exit translate are one pair, one distance, opposite ends

blends.source: the operator's own ask - "literally pushing out one frame with the next, so that you keep some of that congruency"

options.means: The slide's own length: the slide runs over the seconds its SECOND suffix declares (after the direction) instead of its default dial.
The slide: pushed off to the left - the incoming frame arrives from the right.
The slide: pushed off to the right - the incoming frame arrives from the left.
The slide: pushed off upward - the incoming frame arrives from below.
The slide: pushed off downward - the incoming frame arrives from above.

lives.note: the render loop's boundary block - THE SLIDE (slideOn/slideU beside dipIn/bzIn) and its paint beside the suck's; the compiler half is _slide_parts / SLIDE_DIRECTIONS / SLIDE_S, read by parse_exit

callable.why: in SCENE_EXITS and TIMED_EXITS; parse_exit accepts slide:<left|right|up|down>[:<s>] and the engine paints it (goldens slide-mid / slide-landed) - it awaits the operator's watch in motion before a short ships it
